items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: she was making a comeback and she was on tour with Bing Crosby.

ctx.x: Yeah, and then after you’re done it feels weird because a person comes out —

Yeah. It’s a kind of reality check. But I mean this really goes along with the ambition to be a studio musician was just it doesn’t matter who you’re playing with it’s making music. I mean it looks good on the resume to have — that record with Rosemary Clooney was really cool. And I was 24, 25 at the time. It was mid-70s in London and she was making a comeback and she was on tour with Bing Crosby. It was not long before he died. And it was just a very cool experience, you know, playing with somebody of that kind…
And they called you at Apple.

items.title: Laurence Juber interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 21, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: his dad, Perry Botkin Sr. was Bing Crosby’s musical director for 17 years

ctx.x: That’s great. Did you have a time back, I don’t know, maybe in March or something, a certain moment where you really started to believe that this pandemic was serious?

It happened very quickly. It was funny because I saw that there were going to be some travel limitations and I was actually, I was ready to get a new car, and I think it was March 10th I got a Subaru Crosstrek anticipating that I’d probably be doing a lot of driving in California. Because I already had to cancel a tour of Taiwan. And then when I went out to dinner with a friend on the 12th of March and learned that he had a number of colleagues who had been hospitalized because they’d been on a skiing trip to…
Oh yea, the Original Dixieland Jazz Band.
